transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-05-05
Start time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 58 minutes (recording auto)
Attendees: Jordan Hale (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Evan Park (Redwood CSM), Samir Patel (Northbridge Procurement), Laura Chen (Northbridge Legal), Diego Martinez (Northbridge Security), Maya Lin (Northbridge Cloud)

Auto-summary (may be noisy): Preflight to align commercial gate & technical keying; discuss MSA redlines, KMS integration, SLA floor, pilot and billing path.

[00:00] Jordan Hale: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, appreciate the time. We're gonna run through where procurement and legal are on this, align on the stuff that commonly blocks pilots, and then Priya will walk KMS / infra.
[00:14] Samir Patel: Thanks Jordan. Quick context from procurement side: finance wants clarity on the commitment model, and legal's been, uh, reviewing the MSA. We also need to understand the trigger for pricing adjustments if we exceed committed throughput.
[00:30] Laura Chen: Hi all, from legal I just want a short list: indemnity limits, data residency guarantees, and DPA language around controllers/processors. Also curious about audit logs — Diego will cover the security asks.
[00:45] Diego Martinez: Yep, we need to confirm what logs you emit by default, retention windows, and whether we can push a copy to our SIEM. Also, KMS: do you support BYOK with HSM-backed keys?
[01:02] Priya Nair: Great questions. Quick answer: Redwood supports multiple keying profiles — fully Redwood-managed keys, customer-owned keys in cloud KMS with envelope encryption, and an HSM-backed option for Dedicated/Private. We'll show the diagram.
[01:20] Maya Lin: Important for us: any BYOK still needs zero-copy custody if possible — we prefer not to export plaintext keys. Also network wise, can Dedicated be placed in our VPC or do we need a peering?
[01:35] Jordan Hale: For Dedicated we support VPC peering and Private mode; the common pattern is a customer VPC peered to a Redwood-hosted subnet. That allows control plane traffic separation.
[01:48] Samir Patel: On pricing: what's the ramp? For a 2-week pilot we want predictable billing and a cap, otherwise procurement won't greenlight it.
[02:01] Priya Nair: We can do a fixed pilot fee + usage overage cap, or set a burst-enabled Dedicated pool with a soft cap. For evaluation we recommend a fixed pilot prepay that covers baseline and a small overage buffer.
[02:17] Laura Chen: On the MSA: there's a clause about liability cap tied to fees — our counsel wants either a higher cap for severe data incidents or carveouts for gross negligence.
[02:33] Jordan Hale: Understood. Our default is fee-based cap but enterprise deals commonly negotiate to X months of fees or a carveout for security incidents — happy to take that back.
[02:45] Priya Nair: Let me jump into the KMS options — I have a slide. (link shared in chat: https://redwood.example.com/kms-integration)
[02:58] [02:58] Priya Nair: Ok, so option one: Redwood-managed keys — simplest, no customer key ops. Option two: Customer-managed KMS — we do envelope encryption and never see the raw key. Option three: HSM-backed BYOK for on-prem HSMs or cloud HSM with attestation. Each has tradeoffs and different support for Private deployments.
[03:20] Diego Martinez: Quick clarification — with customer-managed KMS, do you ever cache plaintext in memory? We're worried about KV cache leaks.
[03:34] Priya Nair: Short answer: no persistent plaintext-at-rest. The runtime uses envelope keys — plaintext may exist in memory while processing tokens (CPU/GPU memory), but we have strict TLS and memory zeroing patterns. The KV cache term sometimes gets mis-said as K V cache, but it's essentially the model key/value attention cache — we can whiteboard mitigations.
[03:56] Maya Lin: Are there SOC2/ISO attestations we can get during procurement? We need the certs and the auditor contact.
[04:09] Evan Park: We can share our SOC 2 report under an NDA and have an ISO snapshot in the compliance pack. I'll drop links.
[04:20] Samir Patel: For the procurement checklist, we need a diagram of the network, a slip that shows data flow, and the SLA page that lists availability and latency SLOs.
[04:33] Jordan Hale: On SLOs — our Hosted product has a 99.5% availability target, Dedicated can be negotiated to 99.95 with runbook integration. For latency we define p50/p95 token latencies in the bench profiles per model.
[04:50] Laura Chen: When you say "runbook integration" what does that look like legally?
[05:02] Priya Nair: Typically we commit to P1/P2 response times in the SLA annex and provide a postmortem cadence; for Dedicated we can include on-call escalation paths and a runbook access window for our SREs to coordinate.
[05:20] [05:20] Samir Patel: Our procurement team is sensitive about early termination fees vs. minimum commitments. For pilot we want the option to terminate without penalty.
[05:33] Jordan Hale: That's standard — pilots have no long-term termination fees. Committed capacity contracts for Dedicated are separate and we can scope minimums. We'll put that in the commercial term sheet.
[05:47] Diego Martinez: Security: we need an assurance about audit log fidelity. Which fields are included? User IDs, API keys, timestamps, request/response hashes?
[06:01] Priya Nair: The standard audit payload includes tokenized user id, request metadata (route, model, tokens), and an event hash for integrity. We can supplement with full request IDs and forward a streaming copy to your SIEM via syslog/S3 integration.
[06:18] Maya Lin: About data residency: some customers require EU-only storage. Can you pin logging and model KV caches to a region?
[06:30] Priya Nair: Yes — for Private and Dedicated you can choose region pinning so KV cache and logs stay in-region. Hosted can be served from our EU region when requested but may still use global control plane telemetry; we can clarify boundaries.
[06:47] [06:47] Laura Chen: On the DPA: we need processing details for subprocessors. Can you provide a list of subprocessors and their roles?
[06:58] Evan Park: We'll share the current subprocessor list; it's maintained and updated, and we can include contractual assurances via DPA appendix.
[07:12] Jordan Hale: Let's talk about SLAs for the pilot vs production. Pilot doesn't usually carry SLA credits but we can instrument perf targets and share metrics. For production Dedicated, SLA credits and uptime SLAs are in the MSA.
[07:30] Samir Patel: Can you provide an example SLA credit calculation? Procurement wants to know the penalty schedule.
[07:41] Priya Nair: Sure — common structure: below 99.95% you get credits proportional to monthly fee. For instance, <99.95 to 99.0 equals 5% credit; <99.0 to 95.0 equals 20%, etc. Exact bands are negotiable.
[07:58] Diego Martinez: We're also concerned about forensic access in the event of an incident. Can you support eDiscovery or provide read-only export of logs?
[08:11] Jordan Hale: Yes, we can provide exports and a forensics bundle for incidents. That process is usually gated by request/PO, but available. We'll put the logistics in the incident response annex.
[08:26] [08:26] Laura Chen: A redline in the MSA asked to add an escrow clause for model weights — we don't expect Redwood to escrow third-party model weights but need clarity when models are custom?
[08:40] Priya Nair: For open models we don't escrow upstream weights; for custom customer-uploaded models we can discuss a custody approach — usually customers keep their model artifacts in their cloud storage and we access them via secure connectors.
[08:58] Samir Patel: Important: procurement wants clarity on billing account identification and invoicing cadence, and whether pilot charges can be net of credits.
[09:10] Evan Park: We can do netting and a single invoice showing prepay pilot and subsequent usage. We'll align with your AP team on PO process.
[09:22] Maya Lin: Follow-up on KMS: If we bring our own key in GCP KMS, does Redwood ever rotate keys or does rotation remain on the customer?
[09:34] Priya Nair: Rotation policy stays with the customer in BYOK. Redwood will honor rotated keys and support re-encryption hooks; we won't rotate customer keys without customer orchestration.
[09:47] [09:47] Jordan Hale: Okay, let's go through a hypothetical risk matrix — Laura, Diego, maybe call out top 3 legal/security blockers that would prevent procurement sign-off?
[09:59] Laura Chen: For legal, it's vague indemnity caps, unclear subprocessors, and ambiguous data deletion language. We need explicit deletion timelines and certification of deletion.
[10:14] Diego Martinez: For security, key custody guarantees (no key export), audit log fidelity, and tenancy isolation for Dedicated are the top items. If those are addressed, we can move forward.
[10:30] Jordan Hale: Great. Priya, could you outline what we would supply to satisfy those items?
[10:38] Priya Nair: We'll supply: a KMS integration diagram, a dedicated audit log schema, and a tenancy isolation architecture doc including network diagrams and NIC separation. Also, a proposed SLA annex with credit bands.
[10:52] Samir Patel: If we get those documents quickly and Laura's redlines are reasonable, procurement could sign off within two weeks. That timeline depends on pilot success.
[11:04] [11:04] Jordan Hale: On pilot success criteria — what do you need to see? Latency p95 below X, throughput Y tokens/day, and no infra/security incidents?
[11:16] Maya Lin: Specifically, p95 inference latency under 350ms for our typical prompt sizes, sustain 3M tokens/day with <1% error rate, and no critical findings in the security review.
[11:29] Priya Nair: We can target those. For the Dedicated pool sizing we recommend 4x A100 equiv to meet that throughput and latency given model choice — we'll produce a perf estimate.
[11:43] Diego Martinez: About the model: are you onboarding a custom model for us or using a Redwood-verified open model?
[11:50] Priya Nair: For now assume an open model with quantization profile; if you want custom weights we have onboarding steps but that's an additional artifact.
[12:05] [12:05] Laura Chen: On the DPA and right to audit, we need a clause outlining periodic audits and your cooperation — would Redwood accept an annual audit window and support for our third-party assessor?
[12:18] Evan Park: We generally support an annual audit through our compliance pack and can accommodate third-party assessments that are scoped and under NDA; there are standard fees for assessor time.
[12:31] Samir Patel: Procurement also asked about export controls and data egress fees if we access models from certain regions. Any egress fees we should expect?
[12:44] Priya Nair: There can be egress fees for cross-region replication of caches/logs; we'll show the billing impact in the pilot cost estimate. For most customers the pilot fee covers typical egress, but large-scale cross-region replication has additional costs.
[13:01] Jordan Hale: Let's capture the immediate risk mitigations: Jordan will send a redline of the MSA with suggested compromise on indemnity and data deletion, Priya will produce KMS and network diagrams and sample terraform snippets, Evan will drop the compliance artifacts and SOC2 link, and Diego/Maya will share security checklist items. Does that match?
[13:20] Laura Chen: Yes. Add that legal would like a proposed escrow/forensics clause for custom models.
[13:30] [13:30] Priya Nair: I'll also attach an example incident response playbook we use in enterprise deals. It lists timelines for P1/P2 and the forensics bundle we hand off.
[13:42] Maya Lin: On the pilot provisioning — what's the usual lead time to spin up a Dedicated pool?
[13:52] Priya Nair: Typically 3-5 business days once PO approved; for private/on-prem it's longer. For a pre-provision we can reserve capacity earlier to meet your timeline.
[14:05] Samir Patel: Ok procurement note: if we sign pilot PO, what's the cancellation terms? We want refundable prepay if you can't deliver to timeframe.
[14:17] Jordan Hale: We'll add a clause to the pilot SOW: refundable if Redwood misses the provisioning SLA by >7 days, or we provide extra credits.
[14:29] Diego Martinez: One last security point — can we get attestation that Redwood doesn't run customer code in shared kernel space or anything that would enable cross-tenant escape?
[14:41] Priya Nair: We can provide architecture details: containerized runtime with hardware isolation, and for Dedicated private we go further with tenant-pin GPU pools — we'll include attestation language.
[14:55] [14:55] Laura Chen: For the MSA redlines, I'll share annotated comments by Friday and need to see your suggested edits.
[15:06] Evan Park: I'll collect the compliance pack and share the SOC2 link and the subprocessor table after the call.
[15:15] Jordan Hale: Great — any other blockers?
[15:19] Samir Patel: Nothing else, we have enough to move. Procurement will need the pilot SOW and estimated pilot invoice to start the PO.
[15:27] Jordan Hale: We'll prepare a pilot SOW draft and a commercial term sheet.
[15:33] Priya Nair: I'll also prepare terraform snippets for KMS and an example rekey flow.
[15:40] [15:40] Laura Chen: Okay, thanks all. Let's reconvene after the pilot SOW is shared — legal and procurement to circle on the redlines.
[15:50] Jordan Hale: Thanks everyone, we'll send the docs and follow up in the next few days.

Meeting end.

References shared in chat: https://redwood.example.com/kms-integration , https://redwood.example.com/sla-annex , redwood-soc2-nd.pdf (link via NDA)
